title: Framing screen reports the wrong sensor size (1920x1080) for a camera that delivers 4144x2822
summary: Closed by wave 4 and independently re-verified here, not assumed. native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:867-878 now reads the geometry off the simulated camera's own status (`let (advertised_width, advertised_height) = { let camera = get_sim_camera().read().await; (camera.status.sensor_width, camera.status.sensor_height) };` then `full_width = advertised_width / bin_x`), replacing the second hardcoded `4144 / bin_x` / `2822 / bin_y` sensor. Cross-checked every other declaration of the simulated sensor in the tree: simulation.rs:73-74 (SimulatedCamera::default) and device_capabilities.rs:3071-3072 (get_simulator_capabilities) both read sim_frame::SIM_W/SIM_H, and both pixel-size declarations are 3.76 (simulation.rs:75-76, device_capabilities.rs:3091-3092) - so there is no fourth place left for the Framing FOV box to disagree with the delivered frame. The verifier's reversal of the attribution holds: framing_provider/support.dart:105-124 faithfully uses the advertised geometry and was never the liar.
test: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs mod sim_exposure_tests -> `simulated_frame_matches_the_advertised_sensor` (asserts the stored frame's (width,height) equals the camera's own reported (sensor_width,sensor_height) - the invariant, not a copy of the literal). Command: cd native/skotiq_native && cargo test -p skotiq_bridge --lib sim_exposure_tests -> 2/2 pass.
revert_check: Re-done by me, not taken on trust. Reverted imaging.rs:877-878 to `let full_width = 4144 / bin_x.max(1) as u32; let full_height = 2822 / bin_y.max(1) as u32;` -> FAILS: 'the delivered frame must have the geometry the camera advertised / left: (4144, 2822) / right: (1920, 1080)'. Restored -> pass.
caveats: Simulator-only, as the verifier established. Part (b) of the report's proposed fix - have Framing cross-check the advertised geometry against the last delivered frame and warn - is deliberately NOT done: with the generator fixed there is nothing left to warn about, and a warning would be a disclosure, not a fix. The manual path still uses generate_simulated_image (random) while the sequencer path uses sim_frame (an electron model); that is a separate generator-unification item, not a geometry contradiction.

title: Framing sidebar "Equipment" section shows an indefinite spinner for over 20 minutes on first load
summary: Closed across waves 3 and 4 in both halves, and both halves independently revert-checked here. RENDER half: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/framing/widgets/framing_sidebar/target_and_equipment.dart:315 and :408 now pass `skipLoadingOnReload: true` on both `equipmentAsync.when` call sites, so a re-run keeps the resolved rig on screen instead of blanking to the 60px spinner; the status badge's `loading:` branch at :359-374 renders a 'Loading…' row instead of the empty SizedBox the report singled out. CAUSE half: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/framing_provider/support.dart:83-87 narrows the watch to `cameraStateProvider.select((state) => (state.connectionState, state.deviceName))`, so sensor-temperature / cooler-power / exposure-progress ticks no longer invalidate the provider and re-fire its async getCameraStatus round trip. I checked the remaining inputs for a second churn source: framingProvider is user-driven, backendProvider is swapped only on pairing, and activeEquipmentProfileProvider is a plain Provider projecting `equipmentProfilesProvider.valueOrNull?.activeProfile`, so it re-emits only when the profile list itself reloads - none of them tick.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/framing_fov_camera_churn_test.dart (2 tests: telemetry burst must not re-query; a disconnect still must) and packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/framing/framing_equipment_reload_flicker_test.dart (2 tests: a reload does not blank the resolved rig; the badge names a genuine first load). Commands: cd packages/skotiq_core && flutter test test/providers/framing_fov_camera_churn_test.dart -> 2/2; cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/screens/framing/framing_equipment_reload_flicker_test.dart -> 2/2.
revert_check: Both halves, re-done by me. (1) Replaced support.dart:83-87's select with `final _cameraState = ref.watch(cameraStateProvider);` plus the two locals -> churn test FAILS 'Expected: <1> / Actual: <2>'. Restored -> 2/2 pass. (2) Deleted both `skipLoadingOnReload: true,` lines (target_and_equipment.dart:315 and :408) -> flicker test FAILS on 'equipment_card_survives_a_provider_reload'. Restored (git diff back to the identical 33+/1- hunks) -> 2/2 pass.
caveats: The report's shape ('stuck for 21 minutes') was wrong and the verifier's ('flickers, 8 of 10 samples mid-reload') was right; the fix addresses the flicker and its cause, not a hang. Nothing time-bounds getCameraStatus itself - a driver that genuinely never returns would still spin - but no such hang was ever demonstrated and adding a timeout to a driver call that answers in milliseconds would be speculative.

title: FITS omits XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ (and OBJECT) although onboarding collects pixel size
source: reports/coverage/fix5/imaging--framing--guiding.json item 3 (P3). Wave 4 marked this already-correct on the strength of the manual-snapshot path alone; that closure was incomplete.
summary: The Dart manual-snapshot path really was fixed by an earlier wave (imaging_service/persistence.dart:60-63 resolves the unbinned pitch through _sensorPixelPitchMicrons and passes it to FitsWriteHeader). But the SEQUENCER path - the one that writes every frame of an actual imaging run - was still dropping it: api/imaging.rs FitsWriteHeaderRich::from_frame_context hardcoded `pixel_size_x: None, pixel_size_y: None`, and nothing upstream ever asked the camera for a pitch. All three DeviceOps::save_fits implementations build their header through that function, so every sequenced sub landed on disk with FOCALLEN and APTDIA but no XPIXSZ/YPIXSZ - exactly the defect the finding describes, on the files a user actually stacks, while two frames off the same rig disagreed about the same sensor. Closed end to end: FrameContext gains camera_pixel_size_x_um/_y_um (frame_context.rs:229-242); DeviceOps gains a defaulted `camera_get_pixel_size_um` returning Ok(None) so test doubles and NullDeviceOps need not answer (device_ops.rs:238-247); BridgeDeviceOps (sequencer_ops.rs:646-657) and UnifiedDeviceOps (unified_device_ops.rs:1040-1051) implement it off the camera's own status, treating a 0.0 report as 'unknown' rather than writing a zero-sized pixel; build_frame_context_for_save (instructions.rs:3835-3856) stamps it next to the other per-frame driver reads; and from_frame_context (api/imaging.rs:3567-3576) passes it through. The writer already multiplies by XBINNING/YBINNING, which is why the unbinned pitch is what is carried. A driver that will not answer leaves the keywords off rather than inventing a pitch a solver would trust.
test: Three, covering wiring and mapping separately plus the join. (1) NEW skotiq_sequencer instructions::tests::sequenced_frames_carry_the_sensor_pixel_pitch - runs the real execute_exposure against a ScriptedDomeRotatorOps that reports 3.76 um and asserts the FrameContext the FITS WRITER WAS HANDED carries it (not a hand-built context). (2) NEW instructions::tests::a_camera_that_reports_no_pitch_leaves_the_keywords_absent - the honest-absence half. (3) EXTENDED skotiq_bridge sequencer_ops::pointing_tests::save_fits_writes_the_header_from_its_own_frame_context - drives the real DeviceOps::save_fits, reads the FITS back off disk and asserts XPIXSZ == 11.28 (3.76 um binned 3x3), plus rich_header_tests::fits_round_trip_preserves_all_frame_context_keywords asserts 7.52 at bin 2. Commands: cd native/skotiq_native && cargo test -p skotiq_sequencer (728+5+4+12 pass, 0 fail) && cargo test -p skotiq_bridge (468 pass, 0 fail); cargo fmt --check clean.
revert_check: Both hops severed independently. (1) Reverted api/imaging.rs from_frame_context to `pixel_size_x: None, pixel_size_y: None` -> fits_round_trip_preserves_all_frame_context_keywords FAILS at imaging.rs:5850 'XPIXSZ card' (the .expect on the absent keyword). Restored -> pass. (2) Deleted the whole `if let Some(camera_id) = &ctx.camera_id { match ctx.device_ops.camera_get_pixel_size_um(...) }` block from build_frame_context_for_save (instructions.rs:3841-3856) -> sequenced_frames_carry_the_sensor_pixel_pitch FAILS 'left: (None, None) / right: (Some(3.76), Some(3.76))'. Restored -> pass.
caveats: Two things this deliberately does not touch. (a) The missing OBJECT card in the report is not a bug: persistence.dart:68 passes `objectName: targetName`, legitimately null for a manual capture with no session target, and the sequencer path already writes it from ctx.target_name. (b) flat_wizard_provider.dart:1131 builds a third, much sparser FitsWriteHeader (frame type, filter, exposure, timestamp, gain, offset, binning and nothing else) - so flats are missing FOCALLEN, APTDIA, INSTRUME and the site cards as well as the pitch. That is a wider gap than this finding, whose evidence explicitly describes files that DO carry FOCALLEN, and adding only the pitch there would be arbitrary; it wants its own item. Costs one extra camera-status round trip per saved frame, on a path that already makes several (cooler power, focuser position, focuser temperature, rotator angle).
